title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 aims to ensure that any AI tools used in the judicial system are carefully studied and monitored for fairness, accuracy, and reliability. It creates a new oversight body and requires regular reporting on AI performance, bias, and impact on court proceedings.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says that every American—and especially communities that will be affected by building or running an artificial‑intelligence data center—deserves clear, open information about those projects. They also believe these communities should have a say in how the data center is managed, ensuring local control and decision‑making power.

title: To better coordinate Federal efforts to utilize advance technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve diagnoses, treatments, cures, and prevention strategies for pediatric cancer, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The policy seeks to coordinate federal efforts that use advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve the diagnosis, treatment, cure, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It also aims to expand these initiatives to other related health purposes for children.

title: To provide for certain artificial intelligence agent discovery and security standards, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy establishes standards for locating and identifying artificial intelligence agents to ensure they can be tracked and monitored. It also sets security requirements and related guidelines to protect AI systems and their users.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary pause on building or expanding new data centers that host AI systems. Its purpose is to let lawmakers assess the environmental and energy‑use impacts of these facilities before allowing further growth.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is designed to protect AI developers and owners from unauthorized use and theft of their models. It establishes legal penalties and enforcement measures to deter individuals and entities in the U.S. from illicitly copying or distributing AI model architectures and training data.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the construction and operation of AI data centers on federal lands. It aims to protect national resources and ensure that government property is not used for high‑energy, high‑heat AI infrastructure.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 will require companies that develop or use automated decision‑making systems to evaluate the potential impact of those systems on fairness, privacy, and public safety. It will set up a framework for companies to document their risk assessments and report findings to regulators, helping to ensure that AI technologies are used responsibly and transparently.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a legislative proposal aimed at safeguarding elections from manipulation by artificial intelligence. It seeks to regulate AI‑generated content and deceptive practices that could influence voter behavior and undermine electoral integrity.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act is a proposed law that seeks to shield households from rising energy expenses caused by the growing demand of AI data centers. It likely includes measures to regulate the energy usage of these facilities, incentivize renewable sources, and provide subsidies or tax credits to mitigate the impact on family budgets.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 sets rules for how AI systems can be built, used, and monitored in the United States, aiming to keep them safe, transparent, and accountable. It creates standards and oversight mechanisms that balance innovation with protections for people’s privacy, security, and public trust.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: The resolution expresses Congress’s approval of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which aims to safeguard consumers from rising electricity costs. It stresses that protecting ratepayers and promoting affordable, reliable power is essential for households, businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms as the country expands AI and data‑center infrastructure.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 is a policy that sets standards for using liquid cooling in AI data centers to boost efficiency and cut energy usage. It requires manufacturers and operators to follow guidelines that protect safety, the environment, and the reliability of AI hardware.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law that seeks to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies, including the energy use of training models, the generation of electronic waste, and associated carbon emissions. It establishes regulations, reporting requirements, and incentives for companies to adopt greener AI practices and technologies.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate how artificial intelligence systems gather, store, and use data. It aims to protect privacy, promote transparency, and ensure responsible data handling that aligns with public interests.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that use automated decision‑making systems to conduct impact assessments and report on how those algorithms affect public safety, fairness, and privacy. It aims to increase transparency and accountability in AI by setting standards for testing, documentation, and corrective measures to protect consumers and society.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act is a law that safeguards the personal information of children when they use AI systems. It requires AI providers to get parental consent, limit data collection, and follow strict privacy and security standards.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: This act sets new safety standards for AI‑powered toys sold to children, requiring manufacturers to test for harmful content, ensure data privacy, and provide clear labeling and parental controls. It imposes compliance deadlines and oversight to protect kids from potential risks associated with interactive, intelligent toys.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 seeks to create a national framework for developing, deploying, and overseeing AI‑powered physical systems such as autonomous vehicles, drones, and robotics. It establishes regulatory standards, safety protocols, and interagency coordination to ensure these technologies are used safely and responsibly.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act seeks to broaden the range of perspectives represented in AI policy‑making and governance. It calls for increased participation from under‑represented groups to ensure their concerns and insights shape how AI is developed, regulated, and deployed.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on building new AI data centers to address growing concerns about their environmental, energy, and regulatory impacts. The law aims to give lawmakers time to study the industry and create guidelines before allowing further AI infrastructure expansion.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a temporary halt on building or expanding data centers that power AI systems. It is intended to give lawmakers time to assess environmental, energy, and privacy concerns before new AI infrastructure is added.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act seeks to establish guidelines for collecting, managing, and sharing data so that it can be used efficiently and safely by AI systems. It focuses on ensuring data quality, privacy protection, and interoperability, thereby supporting responsible AI development and deployment.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a law that sets rules for how AI can be used in vocational education and training. It aims to make sure AI tools are safe, fair, and transparent for students and educators.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for identifying, assessing, and mitigating risks posed by AI systems, ensuring that developers and users evaluate potential harms before deployment. The act requires entities to conduct thorough risk assessments, document findings, and submit reports to regulators to promote transparency and safeguard public interests.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 is a federal law that directs the National Science Foundation to fund new AI research and educational programs across the United States. It focuses on developing AI curricula, training teachers, and creating research centers to help students and professionals gain the skills needed for the rapidly growing AI field.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 is designed to boost AI research and development through targeted funding, incentives, and collaborative partnerships between government, academia, and industry. It also establishes oversight and ethical guidelines to ensure responsible innovation while protecting public interests and fostering a competitive, forward‑looking AI ecosystem.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act proposes comprehensive rules for developing, deploying, and using artificial intelligence systems. It aims to ensure safety, transparency, and accountability, while fostering innovation and protecting users from bias and misuse.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act aims to help small businesses adopt and develop AI technologies. It provides funding, training, and regulatory support to promote innovation while ensuring responsible AI use.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is intended to provide federal funding and resources to help small business owners and their staff learn how to use artificial intelligence tools and technologies. It establishes a framework for training programs, certifications, and responsible AI adoption so small businesses can remain competitive and innovative in the digital economy.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law aimed at regulating artificial intelligence to keep it safe, transparent, and accountable. It sets out guidelines, oversight, and enforcement rules for developers and users of AI systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is a proposed law that seeks to protect consumers from fraud and deceptive practices involving AI technologies. It establishes rules and penalties for entities that create or use AI for scams, aiming to reduce deceptive use of artificial intelligence and promote transparency.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The States' Right to Regulate AI Act gives individual U.S. states the authority to create and enforce laws governing the use, development, and deployment of AI technologies within their borders. The act aims to ensure AI systems meet safety, transparency, and ethical standards, and allows states to tailor rules to their specific needs.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 establishes new standards to protect individuals from discrimination and violations of civil liberties by AI systems. It mandates that developers conduct bias audits, disclose the impact of AI decisions, and provide a clear mechanism for people to challenge or appeal outcomes that affect them.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 sets out a national plan to grow and support a skilled workforce for AI and other critical technologies. It outlines training, education, and funding initiatives aimed at closing talent gaps and ensuring a pipeline of professionals ready to meet future technological challenges.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act sets rules to stop foreign adversaries from using artificial intelligence to harm the United States or its allies. It requires U.S. companies and organizations to assess AI risks, put safeguards in place, and report potential AI threats that could compromise national security.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act establishes a national program to educate citizens about artificial intelligence, its benefits, and risks. It requires federal agencies and educational institutions to develop and deliver accessible AI resources and outreach to ensure a knowledgeable and prepared public.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 proposes new regulations for the development and deployment of AI technologies, emphasizing safety, transparency, and accountability. It aims to set legal standards for AI systems to protect users and promote responsible innovation.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes guidelines for how the U.S. Small Business Administration and small businesses can responsibly use AI technology. It requires transparency, safeguards, and training to protect consumers and promote equitable access.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: This act proposes rules to oversee artificial intelligences that can change their own behavior or code. It requires regular monitoring, reporting, and safety checks to keep such self-improving systems transparent and safe.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act proposes regulations to assess and mitigate the potential use of generative AI technologies in supporting or facilitating terrorism. It aims to establish guidelines and oversight mechanisms to evaluate risks associated with AI‑generated content that could be used for extremist planning or propaganda.
